newsitem.title: USA: CalPERS seeks Chair/CEO split at Bassett.
newsitem.headline: CalPERS seeks Chair/CEO split at Bassett.

text.p: The California Public Employees' Retirement System (CalPERS), the largest pension fund in the country, Monday said it wants Bassett Furniture Industries Inc to separate the chief executive and chairman positions, as well as name an independent chairman.

In a statement, CalPERS, which uses its position as a large institutional shareholder to seek changes in corporate governance, has filed a shareholder proposal with Bassett's board seeking the two changes.
"We want strong, objective leadership on the Bassett board," said Kayla Gillan, general counsel at CalPERS.

Earlier this month, the Virginia-based furniture maker named Paul Fulton chairman and chief executive to replace a retiring Robert Spilman, effective August 1. Fulton has been a member of Bassett's board and its audit committee since 1993.
A company spokesman for Bassett was not immediately available for a comment on CalPERS' proposal.

CalPERS said Bassett is on its list of underperforming target companies for the second consecutive year. Despite new product introductions in fiscal 1996, Bassett's sales and operating income continued to decline, CalPERS said.
CalPERS met with Spilman and several board members on two occasions over the last two years to discuss separate chairman and chief executive positions.

"In our view, when the board's chairperson is also an officer of the company, it is difficult to objectively perform monitoring and evaluating functions," Gillan said. "We believe an independent chairperson would best ensure the interests of shareholders are served, rather than the interests of management."
